readings.title: Seeking the Divine Direction
readings.subtitle: The remnant approaches Yirmeyahu to ask for the path of harmony, appearing to seek YeHoVaH's jurisdiction.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 42:1] Then all the commanders of the army, and Yoḥanan son of Qarěaḥ, and Yezanyah son of Hoshayah, and all the people, from the least to the greatest, came near [2] and said to Yirmeyahu the prophet, “We beg you, let our petition be acceptable to you, and pray for us to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, for <dn>את</dn> all this remnant, for we are few left of many, as your eyes see us. [3] “And let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> show us <dn>את</dn> the way in which we should walk and <dn>את</dn> the word we should do.”

readings.title: A Vow of Emunah
readings.subtitle: The people declare they will bear the weight of obedience, whether it brings apparent good or evil.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 42:4] And Yirmeyahu the prophet said to them, “I have heard. See, I am praying to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> according to your words, and it shall be that I declare to you <dn>את</dn> all the word <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> answers you. I withhold not a word from you.” [5] And they said to Yirmeyahu, “Let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> be a true and steadfast witness between us, if we do not do according to <dn>את</dn> all the word which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> sends us by you. [6] “Whether good or evil, let us obey <dn>את</dn> the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> to whom we send you, in order that it might be well with us when we obey <dn>את</dn> the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>.”

readings.title: The Premial Offer of Restoration
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH promises to build and plant the remnant if they remain under His geographic jurisdiction.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 42:7] And after ten days it came to be that the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to Yirmeyahu. [8] So he called Yoḥanan son of Qarěaḥ, and all the commanders of the army which were with him, and all the people from the least even to the greatest, [9] and said to them, “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, to whom you sent me to present your petition before <dn>Him</dn>, [10] <dq>If you would indeed stay in this land, then <dn>I</dn> shall build <dn>את</dn> you and not pull you down, and <dn>I</dn> shall plant <dn>את</dn> you and not pluck you up. For <dn>I</dn> have relented of <dn>את</dn> the evil <dn>I</dn> have done to you.</dq> [11] <dq>Do not be afraid of <dn>את</dn> the sovereign of Baḇel, of whom you are afraid. Do not be afraid of him,’</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘for <dn>I</dn> am with you, to save you and deliver you from his hand.</dq> [12] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall show you <dn>את</dn> compassion, so that he has compassion on you and let you return to your own land.’</dq>

readings.title: The Penal Consequence of Defection
readings.subtitle: Fleeing to the crucible of Mitsrayim will only guarantee the systemic devastation they seek to escape.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 42:13] <dq>“But if you say, ‘We are not staying in this land,’ and so disobey <dn>את</dn> the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>,</dq> [14] <dq>saying, ‘No, but we are going to the land of Mitsrayim so that we see no fighting, nor hear <dn>את</dn> a voice of a shophar, nor hunger for bread, and there we shall stay,’</dq> [15] <dq>then hear <dn>את</dn> the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, O remnant of Yehuḏah! Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, ‘If you indeed set <dn>את</dn> your faces to enter Mitsrayim, and shall go to sojourn there,</dq> [16] <dq>then it shall be that the sword which you feared overtakes <dn>את</dn> you there in the land of Mitsrayim, and the scarcity of food of which you were afraid clings to you there in Mitsrayim, and you die there.</dq> [17] <dq>And so it shall be with all the men who set <dn>את</dn> their faces to go to Mitsrayim to sojourn there: they shall die by the sword, by scarcity of food, and by pestilence, and not one of them shall survive or escape from the evil <dn>I</dn> am bringing upon them.’</dq> [18] <dq>“For thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, ‘As <dn>My</dn> displeasure and <dn>My</dn> wrath have been poured out on the inhabitants of Yerushalayim, so shall <dn>My</dn> wrath be poured out on you when you enter Mitsrayim. And you shall be an oath, and an astonishment, and a curse, and a reproach, and you shall see <dn>את</dn> this place no more.’</dq>

readings.title: The Breach of the Vow
readings.subtitle: Yirmeyahu exposes their superficial religious obedience as a self-deceptive snare.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 42:19] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken about you, O remnant of Yehuḏah, <dq>‘Do not go to Mitsrayim!’</dq> Know for certain that I have warned you this day. [20] “For you deceived yourselves when you sent <dn>את</dn> me to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, saying, ‘Pray for us to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>, and according to all that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> says, so declare to us and we shall do it.’ [21] “So I have declared it to you today, but you have not obeyed <dn>את</dn> the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> in all which <dn>He</dn> has sent me to you. [22] “And now, know for certain that you shall die by the sword, by scarcity of food, and by pestilence in the place where you have desired to go to sojourn.”

readings.title: The Rejection of the Prophet's Authority
readings.subtitle: The assertive leaders falsely accuse Yirmeyahu of conspiracy, refusing to submit to the Word.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 43:1] And it came to be, when Yirmeyahu had ended speaking all these words to all the people – all the words of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> their <dn>Elohim</dn>, for which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> their <dn>Elohim</dn> had sent him to them – [2] that Azaryah son of Hoshayah, and Yoḥanan son of Qarěaḥ, and all the proud men spoke, saying to Yirmeyahu, “You are speaking a lie! <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> has not sent you to say, ‘Do not go to Mitsrayim to sojourn there.’ [3] “For Baruḵ son of Něriyah is moving you against us, to give <dn>את</dn> us into the hand of the Kasdim, to put <dn>את</dn> us to death or exile <dn>את</dn> us to Baḇel.”

readings.title: The Return to the Crucible
readings.subtitle: Defying the voice of YeHoVaH, the remnant drags the vulnerable back into the bondage of Mitsrayim.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 43:4] So Yoḥanan son of Qarěaḥ, and all the commanders of the army, and all the people disobeyed <dn>את</dn> the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to stay in the land of Yehuḏah. [5] And Yoḥanan son of Qarěaḥ and all the commanders of the army took <dn>את</dn> all the remnant of Yehuḏah who had returned to dwell in the land of Yehuḏah, from all nations where they had been driven – [6] the men, and the women, and the children, and the sovereign’s daughters, and <dn>את</dn> every being whom Neḇuzaraḏan, chief of the guard, had left with Geḏalyahu son of Aḥiqam, son of Shaphan, and <dn>את</dn> Yirmeyahu the prophet, and <dn>את</dn> Baruḵ son of Něriyahu. [7] So they went to the land of Mitsrayim, for they disobeyed <dn>את</dn> the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And they went as far as Taḥpanḥes.

readings.title: The Hidden Stones of Taḥpanḥes
readings.subtitle: The Sovereign demonstrates His absolute authority by placing Baḇel's throne directly over Mitsrayim's gods.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 43:8] And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to Yirmeyahu in Taḥpanḥes, saying, [9] <dq>“Take <dn>את</dn> large stones in your hand, and you shall hide them before the eyes of the men of Yehuḏah, in the clay in the brick courtyard which is at the entrance to Pharaoh’s house in Taḥpanḥes.</dq> [10] <dq>“Then you shall say to them, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, “See, <dn>I</dn> am sending, and <dn>I</dn> shall bring <dn>את</dn> Neḇuḵaḏretstsar the sovereign of Baḇel, <dn>My</dn> servant. And <dn>I</dn> shall set <dn>את</dn> his throne above these stones that <dn>I</dn> have hidden. And he shall spread his canopy over them.</dq> [11] <dq>“And he shall come and strike <dn>את</dn> the land of Mitsrayim, bringing death to those appointed for death, and captivity to those for captivity, and the sword to those for the sword.</dq> [12] <dq>“And he shall set <dn>את</dn> fire to the houses of the mighty ones of Mitsrayim. And he shall burn <dn>את</dn> them and take <dn>את</dn> them captive. And he shall cover himself with <dn>את</dn> the land of Mitsrayim, as a shepherd puts on his garment, and he shall go out from there in peace.</dq> [13] <dq>“And he shall break <dn>את</dn> the stone pillars of the House of the Sun which are in the land of Mitsrayim, and he shall burn <dn>את</dn> the houses of the mighty ones of the Mitsrites with fire.” ’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Consequences of Spiritual Adultery
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH reminds the exiles that the desolation of Yerushalayim was the exact extraction of justice for their idolatry.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 44:1] The word that came to Yirmeyahu concerning all the Yehuḏim who were dwelling in the land of Mitsrayim – who were dwelling at Miḡdol, and at Taḥpanḥes, and at Noph, and in the land of Pathros, saying, [2] “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, <dq>‘You yourselves have seen all the evil that <dn>I</dn> have brought on Yerushalayim and on all the cities of Yehuḏah. And see, this day they are a ruin, and no one dwells in them,</dq> [3] <dq>because of their evil which they have done to provoke <dn>Me</dn>, by going to burn incense by serving other mighty ones whom they did not know, they nor you nor your fathers.</dq> [4] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> sent to you all <dn>My</dn> servants the prophets, rising early and sending them, saying, “Please do not do this abominable matter that <dn>I</dn> hate!”</dq> [5] <dq>But they did not listen or incline their ear, to turn from their evil, not to burn incense to other mighty ones.</dq> [6] <dq>So <dn>My</dn> wrath and <dn>My</dn> displeasure were poured out and burned in the cities of Yehuḏah and in the streets of Yerushalayim, and they became a ruin and a wasteland, as it is this day.’</dq>

readings.title: The Economics of Self-Destruction
readings.subtitle: The people continue to provoke the Creator, refusing to humble themselves or walk in His Torah.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 44:7] <dq>“And now, thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, ‘Why are you doing this great evil against your lives, to cut off from you <dn>את</dn> man and woman, child and infant, from the midst of Yehuḏah, leaving none to remain,</dq> [8] <dq>by provoking <dn>Me</dn> with the works of your hands, by burning incense to other mighty ones in the land of Mitsrayim where you have gone to dwell, to cut yourselves off and be a curse and a reproach among all the nations of the earth?</dq> [9] <dq>Have you forgotten <dn>את</dn> the evils of your fathers, and <dn>את</dn> the evils of the sovereigns of Yehuḏah, and <dn>את</dn> the evils of their wives, and <dn>את</dn> your own evils, and <dn>את</dn> the evils of your wives, which they have done in the land of Yehuḏah and in the streets of Yerushalayim?</dq> [10] <dq>To this day they have not been humbled, nor have they feared, nor have they walked in <dn>My</dn> Torah and in <dn>My</dn> laws that <dn>I</dn> set before you and your fathers.’</dq>

readings.title: The Inescapable Decree
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH sets His face against the remnant; none who sought asylum in Mitsrayim shall evade the penal system.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 44:11] <dq>“Therefore thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, ‘See, <dn>I</dn> am setting <dn>את</dn> My face against you for evil and for cutting off all Yehuḏah.</dq> [12] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall take <dn>את</dn> the remnant of Yehuḏah who have set <dn>את</dn> their faces to go into the land of Mitsrayim to sojourn there. And they shall all be consumed in the land of Mitsrayim – fall by the sword, consumed by scarcity of food. From the least to the greatest they shall die, by the sword and by scarcity of food. And they shall be an oath and an astonishment and a curse and a reproach!</dq> [13] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall punish <dn>את</dn> those dwelling in the land of Mitsrayim, as <dn>I</dn> have punished Yerushalayim, by the sword, by scarcity of food, and by pestilence.</dq> [14] <dq>And none of the remnant of Yehuḏah who have gone into the land of Mitsrayim to sojourn there shall escape or survive, lest they return to the land of Yehuḏah, to which they are longing to return to dwell there. For they shall not return, except those who escape.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: Trust Placed in the Sovereigness
readings.subtitle: The assembly completely inverts reality, attributing their past economic abundance to pagan worship.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 44:15] Then all the men who knew that their wives had burned incense to other mighty ones, and all the women who stood by, a great assembly, and all the people who dwelt in the land of Mitsrayim, in Pathros, answered Yirmeyahu, saying, [16] “We are not going to listen to you in the matter about which you spoke to us in the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>! [17] “But we shall do whatever has gone out of our own mouth, to burn incense to the sovereigness of the heavens and pour out drink offerings to her, as we have done, we and our fathers, our sovereigns and our heads, in the cities of Yehuḏah and in the streets of Yerushalayim. And we had plenty of food, and were well-off, and saw no evil. [18] “But since we ceased burning incense to the sovereigness of the heavens and pouring out drink offerings to her, we have lacked all and have been consumed by the sword and by scarcity of food. [19] “And when we burned incense to the sovereigness of the heavens and poured out drink offerings to her, did we make cakes for her, to idolize her, and pour out drink offerings to her, without our husbands?”

readings.title: The True Architecture of the Disaster
readings.subtitle: Yirmeyahu corrects their systemic delusion, identifying their rejection of Torah as the structural cause of their ruin.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 44:20] Then Yirmeyahu spoke to all the people – to the men and to the women, and to all the people who had given him that answer, saying, [21] “As for the incense that you burned in the cities of Yehuḏah and in the streets of Yerushalayim, you and your fathers, your sovereigns and your heads, and the people of the land, did not <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> remember <dn>את</dn> them? And it came into <dn>His</dn> heart! [22] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> could no longer bear it, because of the evil of your deeds and because of the abominations which you did. Therefore your land is a ruin, an object of astonishment, a curse, and without an inhabitant, as it is this day. [23] “Because you have burned incense and because you have sinned against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and did not obey <dn>את</dn> the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> or walk in <dn>His</dn> Torah, in <dn>His</dn> laws or in <dn>His</dn> witnesses, therefore this evil did befall you, as at this day.”

readings.title: The Severing of the Guarantee
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH swears by His great Name that it will no longer be invoked by the rebellious in Mitsrayim.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 44:24] And Yirmeyahu said to all the people and to all the women, “Hear <dn>את</dn> the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, all Yehuḏah who are in the land of Mitsrayim! [25] “Thus spoke <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, saying, <dq>‘You and your wives have spoken with your mouths, and have filled with your hands, saying, “We shall perform our vows that we have made, to burn incense to the sovereigness of the heavens and pour out drink offerings to her.” Then confirm your vows and perform your vows!’</dq> [26] <dq>“Therefore hear <dn>את</dn> the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, all Yehuḏah who are dwelling in the land of Mitsrayim, ‘See, <dn>I</dn> have sworn by <dn>My</dn> great Name,’</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘<dn>My</dn> Name shall no longer be called upon by the mouth of any man of Yehuḏah in all the land of Mitsrayim, saying, “As the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives...”</dq> [27] <dq>See, <dn>I</dn> am watching over them for evil and not for good. And all the men of Yehuḏah who are in the land of Mitsrayim shall be consumed by the sword and by scarcity of food, until they come to an end.</dq> [28] <dq>And those who escape the sword, few in number, shall return from the land of Mitsrayim to the land of Yehuḏah. And all the remnant of Yehuḏah, who came into the land of Mitsrayim to sojourn there, shall know whose word is established, <dn>Mine</dn> or theirs.</dq>

readings.title: The Sign of Transferred Authority
readings.subtitle: The fall of Pharaoh Ḥophra is decreed as the physical proof of YeHoVaH's inescapable judgment.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 44:29] <dq>And this is the sign to you,’</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘that <dn>I</dn> am punishing you in this place, so that you know that <dn>My</dn> words are certainly established against you for evil.’</dq> [30] <dq>“Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, ‘See, <dn>I</dn> am giving <dn>את</dn> Pharaoh Ḥophra sovereign of Mitsrayim into the hand of his enemies and into the hand of those who seek his life, as <dn>I</dn> gave <dn>את</dn> Tsiḏqiyahu sovereign of Yehuḏah into the hand of Neḇuḵaḏretstsar sovereign of Baḇel, his enemy who sought his life.’ ”</dq>

readings.subsection: The Physical Proof of the Word
readings.title: The Axis of the Siege
readings.subtitle: News of the city's destruction arrives, lifting the prophet's silence and proving his divine appointment.
readings.text: [Ezekiel 33:21] And it came to be in the twelfth year of our exile, in the tenth month, on the fifth of the new moon, that one who had escaped from Yerushalayim came to me and said, “The city has been stricken!” [22] And the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came upon me the evening before the man came who had escaped. And <dn>He</dn> had opened <dn>את</dn> my mouth, before he came to me in the morning. And my mouth was opened. And I was no longer silent.

readings.title: Claiming the Promise Without the Prerequisites
readings.subtitle: The inhabitants of the ruins assert a birthright while actively violating the foundational instructions of Torah.
readings.text: [Ezekiel 33:23] Then the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to me, saying, [24] <dq>“Son of man, they who inhabit those ruins in the land of Yisra’ěl are saying, ‘Aḇraham was only one, and he inherited the land. But we are many, let the land be given to us as a possession.’</dq> [25] <dq>“Therefore say to them, ‘Thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “You eat <dn>את</dn> meat with blood, and you lift up <dn>את</dn> your eyes toward your idols, and shed <dn>את</dn> blood. Should you then possess the land?</dq> [26] <dq>“You depend on your sword, and you commit abominations, and each of you defiles his neighbour’s wife. Should you then possess the land?” ’</dq>

readings.title: The Eviction from the Land
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH decrees absolute desolation, executing strict justice upon those who defile His territory.
readings.text: [Ezekiel 33:27] <dq>“Say this to them, ‘Thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “As <dn>I</dn> live, those who are in the ruins shall fall by the sword, and the one who is in the open field <dn>I</dn> shall give to the beasts to be devoured, and those who are in the strongholds and caves shall die of the pestilence.</dq> [28] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall make <dn>את</dn> the land a desert and a waste, the arrogance of her strength shall cease, and the mountains of Yisra’ěl shall be a waste, with none passing through.</dq> [29] <dq>“And they shall know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, when <dn>I</dn> have made <dn>את</dn> the land a desert and a waste, because of all their abominations which they have done.” ’</dq>

readings.title: The Illusion of Religious Entertainment
readings.subtitle: The people listen to the prophet as a mere performance, their hearts remaining anchored to the exploitation of the world's economy.
readings.text: [Ezekiel 33:30] <dq>“As for you, son of man, the children of your people are talking about you beside the walls and in the doors of the houses. And they speak to each other, each saying to his brother, ‘Please come and hear what <dn>את</dn> the word is that comes from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’</dq> [31] <dq>“And they come to you as people do, and they sit before you as <dn>My</dn> people, and they hear your words, but they do not do them. For with their mouth they show much love – their hearts pursue their greedy gain.</dq> [32] <dq>“And see, you are to them as a very lovely song of one who has a beautiful voice and playing well on an instrument. And they hear your words, but they do not do them.</dq> [33] <dq>“And when it comes – see, it shall come – then they shall know that a prophet has been in their midst.”</dq>
